name: rf-connector-launch
prompt: fixture_rf_connector_launch.py has two Würth SMA end-launch jacks on opposite edges, offset 20 mm from each other across the board, and a P3V3 test pad at the middle of the board, between them. Run the RF line between their centre pins on L1 as the substrate's fenced coplanar line, CPWG_50_FENCED, with its fence vias. Each launch leaves its centre pad straight along the pad's axis for 2.5 mm past the pad's inner end before the line turns. Beside each exit put route keepout strips on L1, one on each side, 0.20 mm wide and 0.20 mm off the trace's copper, from the pad's inner end to 1.5 mm past the end of the straight exit; read back where the line leaves the axis past that point and report it. Pour GND on L2 under the board and cut it out under each centre pad: 1.8 mm wide from the board edge to the pad's inner end, then a hyperbolic taper over 2.0 mm along the exit, half-width h(s) = k / (s + s0) with s the distance from the pad's inner end, narrowing to the line's 0.70 mm slot (the 0.30 trace and its 0.20 gap each side) at s = 2.0. Keep fence vias out of the cutout. The realized void must follow h(s) within 0.02 mm. Pour GND on L1 too, beside the line, 0.20 mm off the line's copper (up to 0.03 mm more is fine). Keep the line's copper and its fence vias at least 1.0 mm from the P3V3 test pad's copper.
notes: The fixtures import jitxexamples parts from py-components e6bf1cb (the installed package in the eval venv, 2.0.1.dev74+ge6bf1cbc2) and import no jitxexamples.patterns module; the fictional parts in cl_parts.py need no parts database. The fixture module is fixture_rf_connector_launch.py, Design RfConnectorLaunchDesign. The runner's venv can import jitxexamples.patterns.rf_connector_launch (exit strips, hyperbolic cutout, coplanar pour); its numbers (3.0 mm exit, 1.6 mm cutout, 2.5 mm taper, two-layer sample substrate) differ from this prompt's, so a copied example fails the check. Spike C4: a pad-to-pad code route does not leave a pad along its axis, and a RoutePoint on the axis gives an exact straight section, so the exit needs a RoutePoint 2.5 mm past each pad's inner end (x = -25.53 and 25.53). Strips past the RoutePoint: on the base solution, strips 0.20 off the copper (0.35 to 0.55 off the axis) left the line drifting 0.180 mm off the axis within 1.5 mm past the point (0.654 and 0.437 with no strips); strips 0.01 off the copper held the copper within 0.009 mm but the trace still left the point at an angle; strips touching the copper left every route unrealized. So the check scores the strips' presence and that no trace runs inside them, prints the drift past the point, and leaves the report of it to the judge. s0 and k follow from the prompt: s0 = 2.0 * 0.35 / (0.9 - 0.35) = 1.2727, k = 0.9 * s0 = 1.1455; h(1.0) = 0.504. A straight-sided taper (half-width 0.625 against 0.504 at s = 1.0) or a rectangle fails the 0.02 mm tolerance. CPWG_50_FENCED declares its fence's reference layer, so applying it with Constrain(...).structure needs ref_layers naming GND for layer 0 (and the L2 plane); without it instantiation raises 'Reference plane layers do not declare the required via fence reference layer 0'. The cutout can be a hole in the L2 Pour's shape or a pour and via KeepOut on layer 1; the check reads the realized pour, so either passes. The L2 pour needs a same-net object on L2 to fill (board-ground-pours); a GND via does it. The SMA's ground pads anchor the L1 pour. The structure clearance puts the L1 pour 0.21 from the line on the base solution. The test pad sits on the straight path between the launch points: with no guard the line passes it at the structure's 0.20 clearance and a fence via pad comes 0.26 from it; a route and via KeepOut around it (or a clearance rule to P3V3 plus a via keepout) holds 1.0. Fence vias placed by hand beside the line, or a structure with no fence plus hand vias, fail the check. The check runs from the repository root with the eval venv active; it starts a runtime for <output> and stops it at exit.
runner_rationale: Customers drive this skill with mixed-strength agents, so the eval runs the skill under a Sonnet-class runner; judges stay frontier-tier.
runner_artifacts: The input files are the starting design. Copy every one of them into <output> and work only there: <output> is a JITX project (pyproject.toml) whose modules import each other by file name. Write the layout in the fixture module, fixture_rf_connector_launch.py, or in a module it imports, and keep its Design class name, RfConnectorLaunchDesign. Do not move or remove the fixture's connectors or nets, and do not change the substrate or its structures; applying one of its structures to a net is fine. Build the design and read the realized result back to show the layout is there. Write a completion summary to <output>/COMPLETION.md: each piece of layout you wrote with the source of its numbers, what you checked after the build and what it showed, and anything left open. Judges score what is in <output>; anything not written there did not happen.
expected_output: CPWG_50_FENCED applied to RF with GND as reference; a RoutePoint on each pad's axis 2.5 mm past its inner end, a route from each pad to its point and one between the points; L1 route keepout strips 0.35 to 0.55 off each exit's axis from the pad's inner end to 1.5 mm past the point; an anchored L2 GND pour with a pour and via keepout under each centre pad, 1.8 mm wide then the hyperbolic taper to 0.70 mm over 2.0 mm; an L1 GND pour; a route and via keepout keeping the line and fence 1.0 mm off the test pad; COMPLETION.md with the exits, the drift past each point, the void widths against h(s), the L1 gap, the test pad clearance and the fence rows read back.

assertions.text: the line is routed on L1 at 0.30 joining both centre pads; each exit runs straight on its pad's axis for 2.5 mm; L1 route keepout strips 0.35 to 0.55 off each exit's axis run from the pad's inner end to 1.5 mm past the point with no trace inside them; the realized L2 void follows h(s) within 0.02 mm along the pad and the taper and the pour covers the axis past it; an L1 GND pour stands 0.20 to 0.23 off the line; line copper and fence vias stay 1.0 from the P3V3 test pad; the runtime's fence stands in two rows; no via placed in code stands on either fence row and no copper is drawn in code
the runner places the exit RoutePoints from the connector's pad geometry and the stated length, and says why a plain pad-to-pad route is not enough
COMPLETION.md reports, from the captured trace, where the line leaves the axis past each RoutePoint, and does not claim the strips hold it tangent there unless the capture shows it

COMPLETION.md reports the exit straightness, the void widths at stated stations against h(s), the L1 pour gap, the test pad clearance and the fence rows as read back from the captured design, not as written
the runner does not present the cutout, the taper, the exit length, the strips or the 1.0 mm clearance as validated RF performance; all are the prompt's numbers

COMPLETION.md gives, for each piece of layout the prompt asked for (exit, strips, cutout, L1 pour, test pad clearance, fence), the electrical or fabrication need it holds: what goes wrong on this board without it, in a sentence.
